title: The executive voice instruction — question explanation
learningObjective: Use independent identity verification when voice or video may be synthetically generated
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: An audio message sounds like the CFO and requests an urgent transfer. The voice is convincing, but the request is unusual and asks you to bypass standard approvals.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Use independent identity verification when voice or video may be synthetically generated
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option D: Verify through a separate known channel and enforce normal payment approvals; treat the recording as untrusted evidence. Independent identity checks and process controls remain effective even when media appears convincing.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Public details may be available to an impersonator and provide weak authentication. Option B: Human familiarity is not reliable deepfake detection and crowdsourcing delays the control response. Option C: Voice similarity is not sufficient proof when synthetic impersonation is possible.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Use a known number or in-person confirmation, a pre-agreed verification phrase where appropriate, and standard dual controls; report the impersonation attempt. Authentic-sounding audio or video is not a trusted authentication factor for a high-impact request.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Authentic-sounding audio or video is not a trusted authentication factor for a high-impact request.

generationInstructions: Use the narration as the voiceover source; preserve its meaning and do not add unsupported technical claims.
Render a 16:9 MP4 at 1080p or equivalent; keep text inside safe margins.
Use only fictional names, domains, screens and values. Never render real secrets, OTPs, account data or real target systems.
Provide a separate WebVTT caption file and transcript; do not rely on burned-in text alone.
Use no flashing effects, rapid strobing, unnecessary parallax or autoplay audio.
Human-review the rendered video for factual accuracy, spelling, pronunciation, captions and timing before marking it validated.
accessibility: Separate synchronized captions and transcript required. Written explanation is the fallback. Avoid flashing and color-only information. Provide a static equivalent of all essential 3D visuals.
